attempts.summary: Configured node1 (an OPNsense/FreeBSD appliance acting as the private-network's resolver via its built-in Unbound service) to block blocked.example and all its subdomains with a persistent local-zone always_nxdomain drop-in (/usr/local/etc/unbound.opnsense.d/[REDACTED].conf, loaded by OPNsense's start.sh on every boot/reload), while all other names continue to resolve normally. Pointed node2 and node3 (Alpine) at node1 (10.100.40.10) for DNS by writing /etc/resolv.conf and disabling dhcpcd's resolv.conf hook so the setting survives reboots. Verified apex and subdomain queries for blocked.example return NXDOMAIN and unrelated domains (e.g. example.com) resolve correctly from node1 itself and from both node2 and node3. Completed the mandatory restart protocol: captured healthy baselines, restarted node1, node2, and node3 one at a time (preserving no shared quorum requirement since this is a resolver+2 clients topology), confirmed each node's boot identity changed (FreeBSD kern.boottime for node1, Linux boot_id for node2/node3), and re-verified DNS blocking/resolution health after each restart. Node3 took an unusually long time (~35 minutes of polling with persistent "connection reset by peer") to become reachable again after `reboot`, but it did fully recover with all configuration and behavior intact.
